misconceptions.description: Using a character label ('lazy', 'careless') instead of describing the specific observed behavior
misconceptions.trigger: draft assigns a trait to the person rather than naming what happened
misconceptions.feedback: Replace labels with observed facts. 'Lazy habits' blames the child; 'could use more practice on fractions' describes the behavior.

misconceptions.description: Asserting a cause you cannot verify ('obviously did not study') as if it were observed fact
misconceptions.trigger: draft claims to know why something happened with no evidence
misconceptions.feedback: State only what you can observe (the score, the date). You cannot know the cause, so do not assert it.

misconceptions.description: Keeping pressuring or urgent wording that fits a memo but alarms the actual audience (here, parents)
misconceptions.trigger: word choice does not match who will read it
misconceptions.feedback: Match tone to the audience. 'Fix this immediately' pressures parents; 'over the next two weeks' invites partnership.
